home.subtitle: A Clinical Tool for Predicting Cardiotoxicity Risk in Patients with Acute Promyelocytic Leukaemia Receiving Arsenic Trioxide Treatment
home.introContent:
Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is a highly effective chemotherapeutic agent for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL). However, its clinical application is significantly challenged by cardiotoxicity. Adverse cardiac events occur with notable frequency and can lead to prolonged hospitalization or fatal outcomes.

Our free online ATO Cardiotoxicity Risk Predictor addresses this clinical need by integrating data from authoritative studies and real-world adverse event reports.

background.title: Background
background.content: Arsenic trioxide (ATO) is a first-line treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) with excellent efficacy. However, its cardiotoxic adverse effects occur at a notable frequency, significantly impacting patient safety and treatment adherence. This tool is built on real-world clinical data to provide individualized risk assessment support for clinicians.

objectives.title: Research Objectives
objectives.obj1: Integrate arsenic metabolism parameters (iAs, MMA, DMA) with clinical factors to build a cardiotoxicity prediction model
objectives.obj2: Provide clinicians with interpretable risk assessment reports to support individualized medication decisions
objectives.obj3: Identify key risk factors through SHAP interpretability analysis
objectives.obj4: Collect real-world data to continuously optimize model performance

scope.title: Scope of Application

algorithm.title: Algorithm
algorithm.subtitle: Learn about the prediction model and technical methods used

overview.title: Model Overview
overview.content: This tool employs a two-stage modeling strategy: first using Random Forest for feature selection, then using Oblique Random Forest for cardiotoxicity risk classification based on the selected features.
overview.modelTypeValue: Random Forest (feature selection) + Oblique Random Forest (classifier)

feature1.name: Total Arsenic (tAs)
feature1.desc: Sum of iAs, MMA, and DMA; reflects total arsenic exposure

feature3.name: MMA Percentage (MMA%)
feature3.desc: MMA as proportion of total arsenic; positively correlated with cardiotoxicity risk

feature4.name: DMA Percentage (DMA%)
feature4.desc: DMA as proportion of total arsenic; reflects detoxification capacity

feature5.name: Concurrent Cardiotoxic Drug (CT_drug)
feature5.desc: Whether the patient is concurrently using cardiotoxic medications

performance.title: Model Performance
performance.note: Metrics are from the independent test set (ROC-AUC=0.909, 95% CI: 0.861–0.957).

shap.title: SHAP Interpretability
shap.content: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is a game-theory-based interpretability method for machine learning models. Each feature is treated as a player in a cooperative game; its SHAP value quantifies its average marginal contribution across all possible feature subsets, measuring how much it shifts an individual prediction away from the overall model mean. This tool applies Kernel SHAP, a model-agnostic variant using the training set as a reference background (Ponce-Bobadilla et al., Clin Transl Sci, 2024).
shap.positive: Positive value (bar extends right): the feature pushes the predicted cardiotoxicity risk above the model average, indicating it promotes cardiotoxicity occurrence
shap.negative: Negative value (bar extends left): the feature pushes the predicted cardiotoxicity risk below the model average, indicating it suppresses cardiotoxicity occurrence
shap.barPlotNote: Bar length represents the magnitude of influence. The sum of all SHAP values equals the difference between this prediction and the training-set mean prediction.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.limitation1: The model was trained on data from a specific institution; generalizability to different populations requires further validation
limitations.limitation2: Only arsenic metabolism parameters are included; not all potential risk factors are captured
limitations.limitation3: Prediction results should be interpreted alongside the patient's clinical situation and cannot serve as a standalone basis for decisions

q1.question: How do I obtain arsenic metabolism parameters?
q1.answer: iAs, MMA, and DMA values must be obtained from a specialized arsenic speciation laboratory report. Validated analytical methods such as HPLC-ICP-MS are recommended.

q2.question: How accurate are the predictions?
q2.answer: The model achieved an AUC of 0.85 on an independent validation set. However, accuracy is affected by data quality; results are for reference only and must be interpreted alongside the patient's clinical context.
